Hello ggplot community,

I'm using ggplot for creating chloropleths and have the need to plot county names on a state map.  Most names plot beautifully but a few need tweaking.  Tweaking could be made much easier with a locator for ggplot while working with maps.  I put forth this problem at stackoverflow.com and received terrific assistance in solving the problem.  Dwin and Baptise worked together to give me the items to build a function for locator capabilities on a map in ggplot.  It still feels like there's something better as it currently only works with one click at a time.  Is there a better way to approach this problem (maybe even something more universal that works outside of maps) or is this it?

Here is a link to the locator code in my drop box as well: http://dl.dropbox.com/u/61803503/gglocator.txt

Thank you in advance.

########################################
require(maps); require(ggplot2); require(grid)  #necessary packages

county_df <- map_data('county')  #mappings of counties by state
ny <- subset(county_df, region=="new york")   #subset just for NYS
ny$county <- ny$subregion


NY <- ggplot(ny, aes(long, lat)) +    #plot a map of NY state with counties
          geom_polygon(aes(group=group), colour='black', fill=NA) +
          coord_map() + geom_point(aes(c(-78, -73), c(41, 40.855), colour=c("blue", "red"))) +
          scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0)) + scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0))

NY 
############FUNCTION_BEGIN#############
ggmap.loc <- function(object){  #ggplot map locator function
   # print(object)
    x <- grid.ls()[[1]][grep("panel-", grid.ls()[[1]])] #locate the panel
    seekViewport(x)
    y <-  as.numeric(grid.locator("npc"))
    locatedX <- min(object$data$long) + y[1]*diff(range(object$data$long))
    locatedy <- min(object$data$lat) + y[2]*diff(range(object$data$lat))
    return(c(locatedX, locatedy))
}
############FUNCTION_END################
ggmap.loc(NY)  #returns coordinates as expected

########################################

Hi Tyler -

Nice function!

It didn't work when I copied/pasted directly into R (and I didn't check to see why), but I did some editing and got this perhaps more useful version :

ggmap_loc <- function(object = last_plot(), message = FALSE, xexpand = c(.05,0), yexpand = c(.05, 0)){
  x <- grid.ls(print = message)[[1]]
  x <- x[ grep("panel-", grid.ls(print=message)[[1]]) ] #locate the panel
  seekViewport(x)
  loc <-  as.numeric(grid.locator("npc"))

  xrng <- with(object, range(data[,deparse(mapping$x)]))
  yrng <- with(object, range(data[,deparse(mapping$y)]))    

    

  xrng <- expand_range(range = xrng, mul = xexpand[1], add = xexpand[2])
  yrng <- expand_range(range = yrng, mul = yexpand[1], add = yexpand[2])    

  c(xrng[1] + loc[1]*diff(xrng), yrng[1] + loc[2]*diff(yrng))
}

# qplot(xvar, yvar, data = df) + annotate(geom = 'point', x = 3, y = 6)
# ggmap_loc()

I'm sure there is  a more efficient way to do this (i.e. pulling from the object scales directly without having to recalculate them), but this works fine.  It can also apply to any ggplot as you see in the minimal example underneath.

Neat!

david.

  if(n > 1){
    df <- NULL
    for(k in 1:n){
      df <- rbind(df, gglocator(object = object, message = message, 
        xexpand = xexpand, yexpand = yexpand))
    }
    return(df)

}

point <- data.frame(xrng[1] + loc[1]*diff(xrng), yrng[1] + loc[2]*diff(yrng))

It took some work to get all the packages to install and work properly, and the code to run cleanly, but I managed to do it... I'd suggest in the future including code that will all run when copied and pasted into a new R session (this includes loading the data). Also, it helps to know what files go where, and what the working directory should be.

Anyway, I got this to work in ggplot2 version 0.9.0, which should be officially released tomorrow. I think that the problem was solved by the inherit.aes=FALSE argument, which tells the new geom not to inherit the default aesthetic mappings -- those from ggplot(div0A_merged, aes(long, lat, group=group)). The OTc data frame doesn't have those columns, and so when it inherits those mappings and tries to use them, it has problems.

For the new version of ggplot2, I had to change the way color and alpha are specified. There are probably some other small things I forgot...

dev_mode() basically allows you to install development versions of R
packages not yet released to CRAN and keeps them separate from the
official CRAN versions. When dev_mode is ON, the development version
of packages is used; if OFF, the CRAN versions are used. If dev_mode
is OFF, the install_github() lines will overwrite the old versions,
which you may or may not want.

Dennis
